chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from 'Abd Allah ibn Yahya from Hariz from Zurarah who said:

I said to Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him): A slave woman who escaped from her masters went to a tribe other than her own tribe and claimed that she was free. A man seized her and married her. Later, her master caught her, and she had already borne children. He (peace be upon him) said: If the husband establishes proof that he married her on the basis that she was free, her children are manumitted, and the people take their slave woman. And if he does not establish proof, his back is lashed, and his children are enslaved. The third aspect is that the meaning is that they will be free if the price of the children is returned to the master of the girl; that indicates that.
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling for children of a slave woman who marries a free man after claiming she is free?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* illustrates the juristic nuance in Shia fiqh regarding *al-walad li-l-firash* (children follow the bed/marriage) when the mother's status is disputed. It highlights the evidentiary burden on the husband to prove the slave woman's freedom at the time of marriage, reflecting the practical legal mechanisms of manumission and compensation in early Islamic society. The inclusion of a third opinion underscores the scholarly diversity (*ikhtilaf*) within the Imami tradition on whether freedom is absolute or contingent upon financial restitution to the master.
